behavioral_effects: Backend coverage runs measure branch coverage; an untested else-path or short-circuit no longer reads as covered
coverage.xml uploaded to the self-hosted Codecov instance carries branch data (branch-rate, branches-valid, branches-covered)
compatibility_impact: The backend coverage floor changes meaning and value: fail_under moves from 54 over a line-only metric to 52 over the combined lines-plus-branches metric that branch = true produces. This is a deliberate re-baseline for a metric change, not a lowering of the bar — the same suite measures 57.95% line-only and 52.90% combined; the floor sits one point under the new measurement exactly as the original did under its own. The floor's location, the CI command, and make test-cov are unchanged; Codecov uploads now include branch data. tests.json's coverage_floors entry updated to match (kind combined-lines-and-branches, value 52). No API, schema, or interface change.
follow_up: Either give tests.json a real renderer that reads fail_under and coverage.thresholds from source, or move it to manifests/curated and update ownership.json; today its generated location promises a regeneration that does not exist
Once ~1.1 points of real backend tests land, ratchet fail_under back up past 54 on the combined metric
limitations: The floor was re-baselined rather than the suite raised to clear 54 combined (about 1.1 points); the operator chose re-baselining explicitly when the conflict was surfaced

governance/manifests/generated/tests.json is edited by hand: it sits in the generated directory and is registered as generated by that directory rule, but pipeline.render_all does not render it, so no sync can rebuild it — a pre-existing generator divergence noticed here and left as is; the entry was updated so the manifest does not contradict pyproject
reason: Backend coverage is measured line-only, so the reports uploaded to the self-hosted Codecov instance carry no branch data and every untested else-path or short-circuit reads as covered; enabling branch measurement changes the coverage percentage from a line metric (57.95 percent) to a combined lines-plus-branches metric (52.90 percent), which the existing floor of 54 was never calibrated against, so the floor is re-baselined to 52 for the new metric with its basis recorded — same tests, a stricter measure, not a regression
risks: A reader comparing the new 52 floor to the old 54 without reading the comment could see a regression; the pyproject comment and tests.json basis both record the metric change and the numbers on both sides to prevent that reading
rollback: git revert restores branch = false (default) and fail_under = 54; the next coverage run returns to the line-only 57.95%. Nothing outside the repository is affected; already-uploaded Codecov reports keep their branch data.
security_impact: None. Test measurement configuration only; no runtime, dependency, or exposure change.
summary: Measure backend branch coverage and re-baseline the ratcheted floor to the combined metric

validators_run.evidence_ref: CI's unchanged command (pytest --cov=app --cov-report=xml, no --cov-branch flag) now reports Branch/BrPart columns, 52.90% combined against the re-baselined floor of 52; coverage.xml carries branches-valid=1946 branches-covered=569 branch-rate=0.2924 alongside line-rate=0.5796; make test-cov inherits the same config
